to state:

† 328. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM 
AND NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have recei ved complaints regarding the 
adulteration of kerosene in diesel due to the difference in the prices of

THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI RAM 
NAIK): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Steps such as blue dyeing of PDS Kerosene, 
periodical inspection of the retail outlets, introduction of tamper proof locking

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE 
AND INDUSTRY (SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The Government has constituted an Inter-Ministerial Standing Group of 
Secretaries which is monitoring the import of identified 300 Sensitive Items. 
The said list contains certain agricultural products also. A Statement showing 
import of major agricultural products during 1999-2000, 2000-2001 and 
2001-2002 (upto Jan. 2002) is enclosed {See below). Wherever abnormal 
increases in import arc noticed, the Standing Group has been recommending 
increases in tariffs. Thus, for instance, in the budget for the year 2000-2001, 
import of duties on many of the agricultural items, (Chapter 1 to 24 of ITC 
(HS) Classifications of Export and Import Items, 1997-2002), were increased 
to provide protection to domestic farm ers. Duty on rice was increased from 
0% to upto 80% on maize from 0% to 50% on apples from 35% to 50% and 
on wheat raised to 50%. Similarly, in the budget for the year 2001-2002, the 
custom duty on coconut, copra, tea and coffee was raised from 35% to 70%.
